title: TPatchEnumerator: emit or filter 5+ corner DCEL faces
description:
Gap B from the 2026-04-29 audit. On Hand-30k the side-count histogram is [0,0,4,18,39,3,4,1,0,1,3,1,1,0,1,0]. We emit 39 quads + 18 triangles (PATCH-79). The 21 multi-corner faces (sizes 5-15) are dropped silently. Audit each:

- 5,6,7-corner cells: likely real higher-valence singularity wedges or T-junction cells. Emit as n-sided polygon patches OR split into quads. Lyon's paper allows non-rectangular cells in general; only the §6 ¶1 procedure forces 4-sided in the conforming output.
- 9-15-corner cells: probably DCEL boundary-walk artifacts (the outer face of the planar dual graph cycling around mesh holes / handles). Should be FILTERED (not emitted as patches) by detecting that the cycle traverses every node ≥ once or has total parametric perimeter > some threshold.

Likely subsumed by PATCH-44 IF Lyon's α-stopping rule produces a denser graph where most multi-corner anomalies are 4-corner cells in a regular grid. Re-evaluate after PATCH-44.
definition-of-done: Hand-30k side-count histogram: 5-15 corner counts collapse to either (a) emitted as legitimate patches with same characteristic position as 3-valent triangles, or (b) explicitly filtered as boundary-walk with a counter incremented in the histogram dump. No silent drops.
testing-plan: 1. Diagnostic dump in TPatchEnumerator labeling each non-quad/non-triangle face as either OUTER_BOUNDARY or POLYGON. 2. Hand-30k regression: total patch count = quads + triangles + emitted polygons (or = quads + triangles after explicit filter).
